- You can apply for an extension of residence for up to two years after earning an associate degree or higher in Taiwan. [1]
- During this extended stay, you are not restricted by the types of professional or technical jobs you can take, employer qualifications or minimum salary thresholds. [1]
- You can work in any field as long as you comply with labor laws, and after the extended stay ends, you can transition to other residency programs based on a points system or regulations governing foreign professionals. [1]

- If an employer fails to insure a student worker, the employer must pay the labor insurance premium 4 times the standard premium and the employment insurance premium 10 times the standard premium as a penalty. [1]
- The employer must report the insurance and employment insurance contributions to the Labor Insurance Bureau on the day the student worker starts work. [1]
- If the employer fails to insure a student worker, the employer may be fined up to 4 times the standard labor insurance premium and 10 times the standard employment insurance premium. [1]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years. [3]
- You must earn at least 128 course credits in total. [3]
- Your department may require more credits; its curriculum table has the exact number. [3]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) for more information. [3]

- A student admitted on an equivalent qualification from a foreign, Hong Kong, or Macau school that ends at the level of Taiwan's second year of senior high school must complete 12 more graduation credits on top of the usual requirements. [4]
- Military training and PE do not count toward these 12 additional credits. [4]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [4]

- In the first year, you must take at least 16 credits each semester. [5]
- In the fourth year, you must take at least 9 credits each semester. [5]

- International students must take the full‑year 5‑credit course “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” instead of the Chinese (B) course. [1]
- The course does not count toward graduation credits. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Take 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center instead of the freshman Chinese course. [2]
- File for the Chinese course substitution before you graduate. [2]
- This differs from Article 3 of the common-course regulations (5 credits of Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students). [2]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [2]

- Physical education (PE) is required for five semesters: Freshman PE I and II plus three PE interest electives. [3]
- It carries no graduation credits, and you cannot repeat an elective with the same title. [3]
- After the five semesters you may take a 1-credit PE course, which also does not count toward graduation. [3]
- The requirement is stated in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 13. [3]

- A master's degree requires at least 24 credits, not counting thesis credits. [4]
- You must also take at least one graduate course of 1 credit or more at NCU (waived courses do not count). [4]
- The requirement is specified in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 58. [4]
- For more details, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心) at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [4]

- A student admitted directly into a doctoral program must complete at least 34 credits, with at least 18 of those being doctoral-level credits. [5]
- Dissertation credits are not included in the 34-credit requirement. [5]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [5]

- 畢業後可申請延期居留，且每次可申請一次，總延期居留效期最長可達2年。 [1]
- 申請時須於畢業後之翌日起算30日內，向移民署辦理外僑居留證。 [1]
- 若未及時變更居留原因，原居留證將被廢止，可能面臨逾期罰鍰或限期出境等風險。 [1]

- 學士班學生修業期限均為四年，所修學分總數，不得少於一百二十八學分。 [1]
- 各系的畢業學分可能更高，以系上應修科目表為準。 [1]
- 國立中央大學學則 第 13 條: 本校採學年學分制，學士班學生修業期限均為四年，所修學分總數，不得少於一百二十八學分。 [1]
- 如需進一步查詢，請洽教務處課務組 https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw。 [1]

- 如有疑問，請洽學務處服務學習發展中心。 [2]
- 官方公告於 115 學年度第 2 學期頒發學位證書相關注意事項（115 年 2 月 12 日）。 [2]

- 語言中心表示送件前請向系所確認適用版本。 [3]
